transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-12-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Olivia (CSM), Alex (CTO - Northrise), Priya (Eng Mgr), Tom (Infra), Sara (Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may contain errors):
Redwood and Northrise reviewing renewal terms, EU on-prem pilot, capacity uplift and timing. Customer worried about data residency and latency for EU users; exploring Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Agreement to run benchmarks and share security artifacts; Redwood to send pricing + SOW.

Topics: renewal timeline, committed capacity, EU on-prem pilot, latency SLOs, KMS and audit logs, fallback routing, pricing model

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — will keep this tight, goal is to align on the workback for the renewal and the EU on-prem pilot.
[00:12] Alex (Northrise): Yep, hi all. thanks — we got the renewal in the pipeline, need to lock capacity numbers and timeline.
[00:20] Priya: thx, and hi, we also want clarity on how Redwood will handle EU data residency and our KMS — that's non-negotiable for a few big partners.
[00:29] Maya: absolutely. Ravi and I will walk through the options — hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC / on-prem) — and then map to your timeline.
[00:37] Ravi (Redwood SE): quick note, from a perf side we saw Northrise's sample traces; your median token length is ok but the 95th pct is spiky. that drives GPU choice and batching.
[00:50] Tom (Northrise Infra): yeah that's our concern — EU users see latency spikes in the evenings. we need sub-200ms gen latencies for the primary flows, otherwise ARR dips.
[01:02] Olivia (CSM): just to set expectations, we can offer a staged approach: start with Dedicated in eu-west with reserved burst capacity, then move to private on-prem pilot if you need full data residency.
[01:15] Alex: timeline? we want the pilot live before end of Q1 2026.
[01:21] Ravi: technically doable — but two pieces: procurement/contract timing, and the infra work for the on-prem box. for Dedicated we can usually stand up region capacity in 3-4 weeks after contract. on-prem is more like 6-10 weeks.
[01:36] Priya: procurement can move fast if pricing is clear. send a draft SOW and pricing table.
[01:41] Maya: will do. we'll include an annex for the on-prem pilot with hardware options and appliance specs.
[01:47] Alex: good. also curious — how do you handle KV cache warm starts? last time we saw cold starts on models that used heavy context windows.
[01:56] Ravi: yeah, cold KV caches are a cause of spikes. our suggestion: enable prefix caching for high QPS endpoints + a small warmup layer during rollouts. plus continuous batching knobs. we can share a config we call a "warm lane" that biases small batches to avoid tail latency.
[02:12] Tom: can that be automated? we don't want manual ops.
[02:16] Ravi: yes — autoscaling + smart routing can be policy driven; we can set throughput thresholds for pre-warming. there are still edge-cases for sudden bursts, but fallback to a slightly cheaper compatible model is possible so you don't fail open.
[02:30] Sara (Security): on the security front: we need KMS/HSM integration, SSO with SAML, and raw request audit logs for 90 days. is that feasible across Dedicated and Private?
[02:42] Maya: yes. for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS and can ship audit logs to your SIEM. for Private on-prem, we can integrate your HSM and provide local audit collection.
[02:54] Sara: ok, what about SOC2 and ISO artifacts — can you share those before procurement?
[02:59] Olivia: absolutely — we'll send the SOC2 Type II report, pen-test summary, and our encryption whitepaper. I'll add that to the action items.
[03:08] Alex: thanks. pricing model question — do you do flat committed tokens or a hybrid where reserved capacity covers baseline QPS and overage is pay-as-you-go?
[03:19] Maya: common approach is commitment for baseline throughput (reserved GPUs) and per-token billing for overflow. we can show a blended rate across generation and embeddings. also quantization profiles can reduce costs significantly for non-critical models.
[03:32] Priya: how much does quantization affect latency/quality? we can't tolerate hallucination increases on the core flows.
[03:38] Ravi: short answer: the latest 8-bit quantization profiles we've validated retain quality on retrieval-augmented flows; we usually recommend a canary on a subset of traffic. for LLMs with heavy long-context usage, mixed precision sometimes works better. we'll attach quality regression numbers.
[03:53] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[03:56] Priya: ok can we get a bench that shows cost per 1k tokens at our traffic distribution?
[04:01] Maya: yes, that'll be in the pricing pack. can you send the distribution? Alex?
[04:06] Alex: yes; we'll send the 30-day token histogram and the 95th percentile QPS by EOD 2025-12-20.
[04:13] Alex: one more — region routing. we have EU and NA customers; does Redwood support geo-routing with failover to another region with data residency guardrails?
[04:23] Ravi: yes, smart routing can be constrained by policy: route EU requests to EU models; in failover we can route to a compatible smaller model in EU or to NA with a flag, but NA routing would be blocked unless you accept cross-border flows. we can put a hard block if required.
[04:38] Sara: we want a hard block for users in EU by default. any cross-border must be opt-in and logged.
[04:44] Maya: noted. Olivia will include the logging flow in the SOW.
[04:49] Priya: about the pilot hardware — what spec do you recommend for on-prem? we have racks in FRA and AMS.
[04:56] Ravi: baseline pilot: 2x A100 80GB (or equivalent LPU), NVMe cache, 192GB RAM, 2x10Gb NIC with direct peering — that supports moderate QPS for the pilot. for production you'd want a pool of 4-8 GPUs depending on the commit. we'll add a sizing matrix.
[05:15] Tom: ok would prefer a smaller pilot if it shortens lead time.
[05:18] Maya: totally — we'll draft 2 flavors: rapid pilot (2 GPUs, limited traffic) and full pilot (4 GPUs, full traffic).
[05:27] Alex: procurement question — our legal needs SLAs for uptime and RTO for capacity. can you commit to a blackout fallback plan?
[05:36] Olivia: yes, we'll propose SLA verbiage with rolling uptime and a failure escalation path; also a fallback policy where traffic is redirected to a lower tier model to keep app online.
[05:46] Priya: what about warm-up costs? if we need to pre-warm KV caches and lock resources, is that charged as part of the pilot?
[05:54] Maya: we can include a small engineering fee for on-prem appliance setup and a one-time pre-warm window. we'll show both options: included in pilot or invoiced separately.
[06:05] Alex: that seems fair. can you put all of this on a timeline?
[06:09] Maya: yes — proposed timeline:
- 2025-12-18: this call
- by 2025-12-22: Redwood sends draft pricing + SOW + SOC2 artifacts
- by 2025-12-23: Northrise shares compliance checklist and auditors
- 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-07: capacity workshop with SE + infra (2 hrs)
- 2026-01-05 onward: Redwood runs 24h benchmark (start date adjustable)
- Target pilot start: mid-Feb 2026, pilot duration 6 weeks
- Production on EU private or dedicated: end of Q1 2026 (contingent on hardware lead times and procurement)

[06:45] Priya: that's aggressive but okay if we agree procurement moves quickly.
[06:49] Ravi: quick note on benchmarking: we'll simulate your token distribution, run steady-state and burst windows, and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:59] Tom: will you also test failover routing?
[07:02] Ravi: yes, we'll include failover scenarios and cold-cache starts.
[07:07] Alex: competitors — we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI for a while; main reason to stay with Redwood is the operational guarantees and the unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private. but price will be a factor.
[07:19] Maya: understood. we'll show a comparative economics sheet.
[07:24] Sara: one more on compliance — do you support key rotation policies integrated into our KMS? we need rotation without downtime.
[07:31] Olivia: yes, we support key rotation via customer KMS with rolling re-encryption strategies; we'll document the flows and timings.
[07:40] Priya: ok action items recap please.
[07:43] Maya: sure — I'll read out: 1) Maya to send draft pricing + SOW + SOC2 by 2025-12-22; 2) Ravi to run 24h benchmark starting 2026-01-05 and share report by 2026-01-12; 3) Olivia will prepare onboarding playbook and logging/SIEM integration steps by 2026-01-07; 4) Alex to share token histogram and 95th pct QPS by 2025-12-20; 5) Sara to share compliance checklist by 2025-12-23. any changes?
[08:10] Alex: nope that's good.
[08:12] Priya: pls include a short appendix in the SOW about fallback / model downgrade policy.
[08:17] Maya: will do.
[08:19] Olivia: I'll attach the pen-test summary and encryption whitepaper with the SOW.
[08:24] Tom: final thing — can we get an estimate for incremental cost if we go from 4 GPUs to 8 GPUs mid-quarter?
[08:31] Maya: yes, the pricing sheet will include delta pricing and a run rate table.
[08:36] Alex: great. thanks everyone. we should reconvene after you send the SOW; maybe a short 30 minute follow-up.
[08:43] Maya: sounds good. thanks all.

Meeting end.
